TO

IS : 7137 - 1973 SPECIFICATION FOR PORTABLE, HAND-HELD MAINS-OPERATED ELECTRIC MASSAGERS
( Page 10, clause 12.3.11 ) -- Substitute the following for the existing clause: '12.3.11 Endurance Test -- The massager is operated for an operating period of 48 hours under normal load but at a voltage 1.1 times the rated voltage. It is then operated for an operating period of 48 hours under normal load but at a voltage 0.9 times the rated voltage. At the end of the test the massager shall comply with the requirements of 52.7 of IS : 302-1973.'

IS : 7137 - 1973

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR PORTABLE HAND-HELD MAINS-OPERATED ELECTRIC MASSAGERS 0. F O R E W O R D
0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 November 1973, after the draft finalized by the Electrical Appliances Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 Electric massagers are used for stimulating the muscles of the human body. This standard has been formulated to cover the general, safety and performance requirements for portable type hand-held mains-operated electric massagers to ensure personal safety against electric shock, safety against the effects of excessive temperature and fire and reliable operations. 0.3 For general and safety requirements as well as methods of tests reference have been made to IS : 302-1973* which is a necessary adjunct to this standard. Should, however, any deviation exist between the requirements of IS: 3021973* and those of this standard, provisions of the latter shall apply. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers portable, hand-held mains-operated electric massagers designed for connection to supplies at voltage not exceeding 250 V ac single-phase 50 Hz or dc. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply in addition to those specified in 2 of IS : 302-1973*.
*General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances ( fourth revision ). Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

3

IS : 7137 - 1973 2.1 Electric Massager -- A hand-held, portable electrical appliance used for stimulating the muscles of the human body. It includes cables and connectors. 2.2 Normal Load -- An operation of 60 minutes idling with the applicator held in place, the massager being freely suspended in steel air by its flexible cord. If necessary, the connector may be prevented from pulling out by artificial means. 2.3 Applicators -- Specially shaped and padded accessories of the massager, to transfer the vibrations of the massager through contact with the human body. 2.4 Rated Duty Period -- The duration for which the massager is designed to work constantly under rated load without excessive heating up. 3. RATING 3.1 Rated Voltage -- The provisions of 3.1 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 3.2 Rated Input -- The provisions of 3.2 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply with the exception that the rated input shall not exceed 120 W. 3.3 Rated Duty Period--Rated duty period shall not be less than one hour. 4. COMPONENT PARTS AND MATERIALS 4.1 The relevant provisions of 5, 7.11 and 7.12 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply, in addition to 4.1.1. 4.1.1 The wires used in the windings shall conform to I S : 4800 (Part IV )-1968 or IS : 4800 ( Part VIII )-1970. 5. CONSTRUCTION 5.1 Relevant provisions of 7 of IS : 302-1973* in addition to those specified in 5.1.1 and 5.1.2 shall apply. 5.1.1 Massager shall be insulation encased class II type in order to provide adequate protection against electrical hazards. 5.1.2 Massager shall be so designed as to prevent the penetration of dust, body oils and perspiration into places where they might give rise to electrical or mechanical faults. The applicators shall be easy to clean and shall be washable. 5.1.3 The mass of the massager shall not be more than 1 kg.
*General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances (fourth revision). Specification for enamelled round winding wires: Part IV Wire with high mechanical properties. Specification for enamelled round winding wires: Part VIII Wires with good dielectric properties under humid conditions.

4

IS : 7137 - 1973

6 . DESIGN 6.1 The massagers shall meet requirements of 6.1 of IS : 302-1973*. 6.2 The design shall ensure that the amplitude of the vibration is controllable in all directions of vibrations. 6.3 The design shall ensure that extension shafts and applicators do not become live even in the event of the failure of functional insulation of the windings due to burning out of the armature. 6.4 Sharp edges which may prove a hazard in use shall be avoided in both the massagers and the applicators. 7. GENERAL AND SAFETY REQUIREMENTS 7.1 Protection Against Electric Shock -- Provisions of 8 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.2 Temperature Limit -- The temperature limits specified in Table 3 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.3 Electrical Insulation -- The provisions of 11 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.4 Moisture Resistance -- The provisions of 13 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.5 Mechanical Strength -- The provisions of 15 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.6 Abnormal Operation -- The provisions of 16 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.7 Operation Under Overload Condition -- The provisions of 18 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.8 Supply Connections 7.8.1 Connecting Facilities Required -- The provisions of 20.1 and 20.2 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.8.2 Service Cord -- The massager shall be provided with a minimum length of 4 m of circular or parallel twin flexible cord. The flexible cord shall be of the PVC insulated parallel twin type, that is, two conductors laid parallel and insulated simultaneously with PVC insulation. 7.8.2.1 The cable shall conform to IS : 694 ( Part I )-1964.
*General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances (fourth revision). Specification for PVC insulated cables (for voltages up to 1 000 V ) : Part I With copper conductors (revised).

5

IS : 7137 - 1973 7.8.3 Cord Grip -- The provisions of 20.12 to 20.15 of I S : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.9 Terminals - The provisions of 21 except that of 21.3 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.10 Screws and Connections -- The provisions of 23 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.11 Temperature Rise -- Provisions of 10 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 7.11.1 The surface temperature of the massager and its applicators when in operation under normal load conditions shall not be more than 5�C above the ambient temperature. 8. PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 8.1 Operations at Overvoltage and Undervoltage -- The massager shall operate satisfactorily at the overvoltage and undervoltage as specified below: Rated Voltage Single value Range of voltage 9. ENDURANCE 9.1 The massager shall be so designed and constructed as to prevent in extended normal use any electrical or mechanical failure. In addition, the insulation shall not be damaged and contacts and connections shall not work loose due to heating, vibration, etc. 10. MECHANICAL HAZARDS AND STABILITY 10.1 Provisions of 14 of IS: 302-1973* do not apply to the applicators. However, they do apply to moving mechanisms of the massager. 10.2 Hooks and/or stands shall be provided for a safe resting position of the massager while not in use. 11. MARKING 11.1 The provision of 25 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply.
*General and safety requirement! for household and similar electrical appliances (fourth revision).

Overvoltage Undervoltage Rated voltage + 10 percent Rated voltage - 10 percent Maximum voltage of the Minimum voltage of the range - 10 percent range + 10 percent

IS : 7137 - 1973
11.1.1 The massager may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark.
NoTE -- The use of the ISI Certification Mark if governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI mark on products covered by an. Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

12. TESTS

12.1 Categories of Tests
12.1.1 Type Tests -- The tests specified in Table 1 shall constitute type tests and shall be carried out on five samples of the same model, type and ratings ( selected preferably at random from a regular production lot).
TABLE 1 SCHEDULE OF TESTS CLAUSE REFERENCE SL TESTS No. 12.3.1 1 Visual examination and inspection 2 Cord grip 12.3.2 12.3.3 3 Withdrawal pull 4 High voltage 12.3.4 44.3 of I S : 302-1973* 5 Insulation resistance (dry) 6 Protection against electric shock 12.3.5 7 Leakage current 12.3.6 8 Moisture resistance 43 of I S : 302-1973* 12.3.7 9 Operation at overvoltage and undervoltage 10 Temperature limit 12.3.8 11 Mechanical strength 12:3.9 12 Abnormal operation 12.3.10 50.4 and 50.5 of I S : 302-1973* 13 Operation under overload condition 12.3.11 14 Endurance 35 15 Screws, connections and terminals 37 of IS : 302-1973 16 Resistance to rusting 29 17 Fire resisting properties 18 Input 12.3.12 51 of IS : 302-1973* 19 Starting (for motorised massagers) 12.3.13 20 Performance 32 of IS:302-1973* 21 Mechanical hazards and stability *General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances (fourth revision).

7

IS : 7137 - 1973 12.1.1.1 Criteria of approval -- All samples shall successfully pass all the type tests for proving conformity with the requirements of this standard. Should any of the samples fail in any of the type tests, the testing authority at its discretion may call for fresh samples not exceeding twice the original number and subject them again to all tests in which failure occurred. No single failure shall be permitted in the repeat test( s ). 12.1.2 Acceptance Tests -- The following shall constitute acceptance tests: Clause Reference Test 12.3.1 a) Visual examination and inspection b) Test for protection against electric shock 12.3.5 42.3 c) High voltage test of I S : 302-1973* 44.3 d) Test for insulation resistance ( dry ) e) Test for leakage current 12.3.6 12.3.7 f) Test for operation at overvoltage and undervoltage 43 of I S : 302-1973* g) Test for moisture resistance 12.3.8 h) Test for temperature limit 12.3.13 j ) Test for performance 50.3 of I S : 302-1973* k) Operation under overload 47.7 to 47.9 of IS : 302-1973* m) Abnormal operation n) Input 12.3.12 51 of I S : 302-1973* p) Starting 12.1.2.1 A recommended sampling procedure is specified in Appendix A. 12.1.3 Routine Tests -- The following shall constitute routine tests: Clause Reference Test 12.3.1 a) Visual examination and inspection 12.3.5 b) Test for protection against electric shock c) High voltage test 42.3 of I S : 302-1973* 44.3 d) Test for insulation resistance ( dry ) 12.3.12 e) Input 51 of I S : 302-1973* f) Starting
NOTE 1 -- High voltage test as a routine test may comprise the flash test specified in 42.3.3 of IS : 302-l973*. NOTE 2 -- Insulation resistance ( dry ) test as routine test may be done without any conditioning. *General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances ( fourth revision ).

8

IS : 7137 - 1973 12.2 General Conditions for Tests -- Unless specified otherwise in the relevant clauses, the conditions specified in 26 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 12.3 Schedule of Tests -- Schedule of type tests to be carried out on the electric massager for proving conformity with the requirements of this standard is given in Table 1 with suitable reference to relevant clauses of this standard and those of IS : 302-1973*. 12.3.1 Visual Examination and Inspection -- The massager shall be visually examined and inspected for conformity with the relevant requirements specified in 4, 5, 6 and 7. 12.3.2 Cord Grip Test -- The flexible cord of a massager not provided with an appliance inlet, when correctly fixed as in service shall withstand a direct pull of 75 N repeated twice, and the flexible cord shall not move noticeably in the cord grip. For all types of terminations including soldered and crimped the conductors of the supply cord sliall not be connected to the terminals during the test. The above test shall also be applied to the grip of the flexible cord to the supply plug, when provided, and in the case of a detachable flexible cord to the connector. When the connection is moulded on to the flexible cord, the connectors used shall not be disconnected and in tliis case there shall be no interruption of the continuity of either conductor. 12.3.3 Test for Withdrawal Pull -- Neglecting previous insertions and withdrawals the connector is inserted and withdrawn from the appliance-inlet 23 times. The pull necessary to withdraw the connector from the applianceinlet during five further withdrawals shall not exceed 50 N nor be less than 10 N when any locking device is made inoperative. The connector shall be inserted and withdrawn from the appliance inlet for a further 65 operations and the pull necessary to withdraw the connector from the appliance inlet for the next five withdrawals shall be not less than 10 N when any locking device is made inoperative. 12.3.4 High Voltage Test -- High voltage test shall be carried out in accordance with 42.3 of IS : 302-1973*. 1.2.3.5 Test for Protection Against Electric Shock -- Test shall be performed in accordance with 40 of IS : 302-1973*, with the exception that the accessibility test with a test pin shall be performed without the connector being removed in case of massager with an appliance coupler.
* General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances ( fourth revision ).

9

IS : 7137 - 1973 12.3.6 Test for Leakage Current -- This test shall be carried out in accordance with 42 of IS : 302-1973* after being operated for a period of 10 minutes, under conditions of normal load ( see 2.2 ). 12.3.7 Test for Operation at Overvoltage and Undervoltage -- The massager shall be checked for compliance with the requirements of 8.1 by applying the voltage specified therein, under conditions of normal load. 12.3.8 Test for Temperature Limit  The test shall be carried out as specified in 41 of IS : 302-1973*. The massager shall be run under normal load conditions. 12.3.9 Mechanical Strength Test  The test shall be carried out in accordance with 36 of IS : 302-1973*. 12.3.10 Abnormal Operation Test -- The test shall be performed in accordance with 47.7 to 47.9 of IS : 302-1973*. 12.3.11 Endurance Test -- Massager is operated at the voltage used for the temperature limit test under 12.3.8 under the conditions of normal load. The period of operation is 60 minutes followed by a rest of 10 minutes. One thousand cycles of operation are performed. After this test the massager shall comply with the requirements of 52.7 of IS : 302-1973*. 12.3.12 Test for Input -- The massager shall be tested with a standard wattmeter. It is operated for a period of 10 minutes at 110 percent of the rated voltage after reaching the full speed or vibrations under condition of normal load. The results shall not vary by more than � 1 0 percent of the rated input specified in 3.2. 12.3.13 Test for Performance -- Under consideration.

APPENDIX A ( Clause 12.1.2.1 )
SAMPLING PROCEDURE FOR ACCEPTANCE TESTS A-1. LOT A-1.1 In any consignment, all electric massager of the same make, model and type and manufactured under similar conditions of production shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.
*General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances ( fourth revision ).

10

IS : 7137 - 1973 A-2. SELECTION OF SAMPLES A-2.1 From each lot, a certain number of electric massagers as prescribed in Table 2 shall be selected at random and subjected to acceptance tests specified in 12.1.2. A-2.2 The number of massagers to be selected depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with col 2 of Table 2. A-2.2.1 If required for repeat test(s) ( see A-3.2 ), additional massagers as given in col 3 of Table 2 shall also be selected at random.
TABLE 2 SAMPLES AND CRITERION FOR CONFORMITY
L O T SIZE FIRST SAMPLE N1 SECOND SAMPLE ACCEPTANCE NUMBER C1 REJECTION NUMBER

(1) U p to 50 51 ,, 100 101 ,, 200 201 ,, 300 301 ,, 500 501 and above

(2) 5 7 10 13 20 25

N2 (3) 10 14 20 20 40 50

C2 (5) 2 2 3 3 4 5

(4) 0 0 0 0 0 1

A-3. CRITERION FOR CONFORMITY A-3.l The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements or acceptance tests, if the number of failures in the first sample N1 is less than of equal to acceptance number C1 given in col 4 of Table 2. If the number of failures is greater than or equal to the rejection number C2 given in col 5 of Table 2, the lot shall be considered as not conforming to the requirements of the acceptance tests. A-3.2 If the number of failures is between C1 and C2 and a second sample N2 shall be selected and subjected to the acceptance tests. If the number of failures in the two samples combined is less than C2 the lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of the acceptance tests, otherwise not.
